subtitle: Most weak posts lose attention before the useful part ever appears.

steps.title: Lead with the tension
steps.description: Open with the problem, result or disagreement that earns the next line.

steps.title: Show proof immediately
steps.description: Use a firsthand result, concrete example or source before making a broad claim.

steps.title: Make one useful point
steps.description: Give each section one job so the reader never has to untangle the lesson.

steps.title: Cut every repeat
steps.description: Remove setup, summaries and filler that restate something the reader already knows.

steps.title: End with one action
steps.description: Ask for one clear next step that follows naturally from the value delivered.

caption: Useful information is not automatically useful content. If the proof is buried, the copy repeats itself, or the post asks for several actions, the reader leaves before reaching the value. This infographic is a five-part editing checklist for making a useful post easier to notice and act on.
